title: report.filed
description: Published by Report Service when a user files a report against another user. Report Service itself computes and publishes the escalation decision (see the `escalated` property) synchronously, before this event is even built — Admin Service (Phase 10) only ever reads the already-decided flag, it does not derive escalation itself.
_comment_threshold: report_count_for_target is denormalised into this event so Admin Service can apply its OWN independent logic (e.g. queue aggregation) without querying Report Service's database. Each service owns its data — Admin reads a summary, not raw rows (Database per Service principle).
_comment_dlq: If the outbox relay fails to publish this event after 3 retries, it routes to report.filed.dlq for manual inspection. Safety reports must not be silently lost.

reason.description: Report category selected by the reporter.

report_count_for_target.description: Total number of reports filed against reported_id (including this one). Report Service uses this, against its own report.escalation.threshold config, to compute `escalated` below. Rating Service independently reads this same raw count against its own unrelated rating.report.suspension.threshold to decide when to recalculate trust score — two services, two independently configurable policies off the same number.

escalated.description: T053: true when report_count_for_target met or exceeded Report Service's own report.escalation.threshold at the moment this report was filed. Computed and decided by Report Service BEFORE this event is serialized — every historical Report document for reported_id is bulk-updated to status ESCALATED in the same write. Consumers (Admin Service, Phase 10) read this as an already-decided fact; they never re-derive it from report_count_for_target themselves.
